Maya (PM): quick sync — we need a decision on routing + fallback parity for EU enterprise tier. I uploaded a compatibility grid but want a short review here first. <https://redwood/internal/compat-grid|compat-grid>
Alex (eng): skimming — main risks are tokenizer mismatch and tool-calling signature differences between v1/v2 variants.
Priya (infra): also quota enforcement: if we fallback to cheaper variant we must still honor tenant rate limits and quota counters across variants.
Jorge (ml): tokenizer note: v1 uses BPE with 4096 context, v2 uses spm with 8192. That means prompt truncation behavior will differ. We should record deterministic behavior for prefix caching.
Sam (sre): +1 on quotas. We can't double-count tokens if we route across variants. Need idempotent counters.
Maya (PM): Alex, can you propose how the router signals to billing/quotas when it does a fallback? Small payload or event? Need to be compatible with existing telemetry dashboard.
Alex (eng): propose: router emits a single routed_request event with fields: tier, region, variant_from, variant_to, fallback_reason. Billing reads routed_request.variant_to for charge rates. Example payload:
```
{ "tenant_id": "t-123", "tier":"enterprise", "region":"eu-west-1", "variant_to":"gptx-512q-v2", "variant_from":"gptx-512q-v1", "fallback_reason":"capacity" }
```
Priya (infra): that works but we must ensure last-mile delivery to billing is async-safe. If router fails to emit, billing should fallback to charged_variant_lookup which maps request meta -> default price.
Jorge (ml): on tokenizer parity: if fallback_to has longer context, fine. If shorter, we need to re-chunk or reject. Prefer: router should avoid fallback to shorter-context variant for requests with explicit max_tokens or long prompts. Suggest rule: only fallback if min(context_len_of_candidate, original_context_len) >= requested_seq_len - allowed_shrink.
Sam (sre): allowed_shrink? that's a policy knob. Maybe default allowed_shrink = 256 tokens for soft truncation; but enterprise contracts might require "no-truncate" option.
Maya (PM): contracts do have "preserve full context" add-on. If tenant has that flag, router must never fallback to shorter-context variant. Add to grid.
Alex (eng): tool-calling parity: v1 uses positional args for functions, v2 uses named args and stricter JSON schema. If we fallback, we need runtime shim that translates v1->v2 call format or vice versa.
Jorge (ml): runtime shim idea is ok but expensive. We should only enable shim for vetted functions (tool whitelist) and record transformation in telemetry: transform_applied: true.
Priya (infra): and we need schema versioning in traces so that logs correlate with function signatures. Add fields: tool_schema_version, transformed_by_shim (bool).
Maya (PM): Dashboard impact: product wants per-tenant metric "fallback_rate_by_reason" + "avg_token_delta_post_fallback". Can we compute avg_token_delta from events?
Alex (eng): yes if router emits both original_token_count and final_token_count. Then dashboard query: avg(final - original) grouped by tenant/variant/reason.
Sam (sre): watch out for privacy — don't log full prompts. Only token counts and hashed prompt ids.
Jorge (ml): edge case: some model variants have deterministic vs nondeterministic tool-calling behavior (signature ordering). We should mark those variants as incompatible for automatic fallback unless shim exists.
Maya (PM): action items: 
- Alex: add fields to routed_request event + implement shim whitelist config (due EOD)
- Priya: ensure billing fallback path exists and is tested (due tomorrow)
- Jorge: annotate model catalog with context_len, tokenizer_type, tool_signature_mode (named/positional) (due EOD)
- Sam: update telemetry dashboard queries and add alert if fallback_rate > 5% for any enterprise tenant (due tomorrow)
Alex (eng): quick question — how to present this in the rollout UX? Users need visibility and opt-out. Maybe show "Prefer performance fallback" toggle per route.
Maya (PM): yes, console should show: current routing policy, fallback_allowed (bool), allowed_shrink tokens, shim_enabled (list). We'll add a new card under Per-Tenant > Routing.
Priya (infra): test plan: simulate requests that hit capacity and ensure variant transitions preserve quota + emit events. I'll set up a canary in eu-west-1.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/routing-fallback-2026-03-18 -> eu-west-1
Alex (eng): FYI: sample config snippet for router rules:
```
- match: { tier: enterprise, region: eu-west-1 }
  allow_fallback: true
  max_allow_shrink: 256
  shim_whitelist: ["payment_check", "lookup_user"]
```
Maya (PM): thanks all. If nobody objects I'll lock grid with these rules and circulate to legal for contract flagging.
Jorge (ml): no objections from me. +1
Sam (sre): ok from SRE.
Alex (eng): fine. I'll open PR for telemetry schema.
Priya (infra): I'll add billing integration test cases.
Maya (PM): assigning tasks in linear. End thread.
